reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence of target engagement for TAK-700. Testosterone suppression was achieved (17.36 ng/dL vs 86.47 ng/dL in control), demonstrating CYP17A1 inhibition worked as intended. Delayed testosterone recovery (HR 0.51, p=0.0104) further confirms target engagement. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: The intended mechanism (androgen synthesis inhibition) was successfully activated - testosterone levels were suppressed, confirming the CYP17A1 → androgen synthesis pathway was modulated. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Despite confirmed target engagement and pathway modulation, the primary endpoint (biochemical failure) was not met. HR 0.83 (95% CI: 0.47-1.48), p=0.55 shows no significant benefit. This represents a biology_moved_endpoint_flat pattern. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No differential responses across racial or ethnic subgroups were observed. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial was adequately powered with 239 patients and 2-year treatment duration. However, significant toxicity was observed (58.9% vs 34.9% grade 3+ AEs, p<0.001) which may have limited the therapeutic window, though this didn't prevent completion of the planned treatment duration.

failure_modes.evidence: Target engagement confirmed by testosterone suppression (17.36 vs 86.47 ng/dL) and delayed recovery (HR 0.51, p=0.0104), but primary endpoint biochemical failure showed no benefit (HR 0.83, p=0.55)
Significantly higher grade 3+ adverse events (58.9% vs 34.9%, HR 2.29, p<0.001) including cardiac events, though planned dose and duration were completed
